audit.whatIsWrong: Rated EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 71.43% win rate over 21 games, with every prose block describing a lane Graves takes over.
audit.why: The page tells you to expect a coin flip in the matchup you win most often on the champion.
audit.corrected: FAV at 4/10; Kled carry threat left at 6/10, which is honest — he does out-scale.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Kled levels 3, 4-5 and first item in both layers, and gives Graves level 1. The packet chart and every why say the reverse: Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Kled.
audit.why: whys[3] says 'you win every extended trade against a pre-item Kled' while the chart directly above it says Kled owns levels 4-5. whys[0] and the early block both call level 1 a coin flip, and the chart calls it a Graves win.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group, and the spikes rewritten around real numbers: Bear Trap's 11s, Quickdraw's 16s, Collateral Damage's 100s and Chaaaaaaaarge!!'s 110-140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications. (a) Smoke Screen is called a blind that makes Skaarl's autos miss — it reduces sight range and slows on impact, nothing in it causes a miss. (b) Graves' Q is described as a 'powder trail' you detonate — Riot's text is a single explosive shell that detonates after 1 second or on terrain contact; there is no trail and no separate detonation. (c) Collateral Damage is twice described as a self-escape 'fired at the wall behind you' that gets Graves out of Chaaaaaaaarge!! — his R does not displace him at all. Only his passive knocks back, and only non-champions.
audit.why: All three are checkable against Riot's own descriptions, and all three change what a player does: holding a trade for a blind that never lands, aiming a shell as if it left a trail, and planning an escape that does not exist are each a lost fight.
audit.corrected: Blind replaced with the slow and sight cut; the Q restated as a shell with a 1-second fuse that detonates early on terrain; the R's real property used instead — the shell explodes in a cone after hitting the first champion, so it still catches Kled charging past.

audit.whatIsWrong: True Grit is described as 'armor from staying in combat'.
audit.why: Quickdraw grants two stacks specifically when Graves dashes TOWARD an enemy champion, and autos refresh it and cut the cooldown. That distinction is the whole trading pattern: dash at him, not away.
audit.corrected: Stated as the dash-toward rule in whys[3] and phases[3].

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: Kled is a real level-1 bully — his Bear Trap yank beats a blind trade, so respect the rope and farm.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: Quickdraw online at 16s — dash in for the point-blank spread the instant Bear Trap is on its 11s cooldown, then out.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: Full kit: End of the Line detonates after 1s or early on terrain — bait the rope, then unload.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Bear Trap on a Rope; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: True Grit stacks two at a time when you dash AT him and autos refresh it — you win every extended trade on a pre-item Kled.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Collateral Damage's cone carries past him — hold it as the execute on a dismounted Kled, never for chip.

edits.before: First item spike — the point-blank Q-AA-E-AA pattern now removes half bars. Force fights near walls.
edits.after: First item spike lands while his courage meter is short — force the all-in before he stacks two.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: Chaaaaaaaarge!! is a 110s engage with a shield — let your team eat it and play for smoke picks.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Kled carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Kled carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Kled carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke cuts sight range and slows on impact — drop it on the gank's arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save R as either the execute or the peel knockback. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.
edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage for the slow and sight cut, dash AT them for the grit stacks, and save R as the execute. His remount out-sustains you — picks don't care.

edits.before: Hold R as the disengage knockback
edits.after: Hold R as the execute on a dismount

edits.before: With Q, W and E you smoke-blind his Skaarl autos and detonate the powder trail — one combo out-trades a Kled who whiffed his rope.
edits.after: With Q, W and E you slow him under Smoke Screen and land End of the Line point-blank — one combo out-trades a Kled who whiffed his rope.

edits.before: Quickdraw's armor from staying in combat plus your refreshing E charges compound, so you win every extended trade against a pre-item Kled.
edits.after: Dashing AT him gives Quickdraw two True Grit stacks and your autos refresh them, so you win every extended trade against a pre-item Kled.

edits.before: Collateral Damage nukes him out of a won fight and, fired at a wall, escapes his Chaaaaaaaarge!! engage — your cleanest kill window.
edits.after: Collateral Damage nukes him out of a won fight, and its cone still lands if he charges past you — your cleanest kill window at 100s.

edits.before: Kled out-scales you: at two items his remount HP and grab damage ignore the armor you build, so let your team handle his R engage instead of soloing him.
edits.after: Kled out-scales you: at two items a full remount plus Chaaaaaaaarge!!'s shield outlasts your two-round reload, so let your team handle his engage instead of soloing him.

edits.before: Q powder trail plus your point-blank shell spread comes online — punish the moment his Bear Trap on a Rope whiffs, since the grab is his only hard engage.
edits.after: End of the Line plus your point-blank shell spread comes online — punish the moment his Bear Trap on a Rope whiffs, since the 11s grab is his only hard engage.

edits.before: Collateral Damage turns a won trade into a kill, and fired at the wall behind you it doubles as your escape from his Chaaaaaaaarge!! engage — your hardest all-in window.
edits.after: Collateral Damage turns a won trade into a kill, and its shell explodes in a cone past the first champion it hits, so it still catches him mid-Chaaaaaaaarge!! — your hardest all-in window.

edits.before: Kled's remount HP and grab damage scale past your armor and his sustain outlasts your reloads — close the lane before he stacks two items.
edits.after: A full Skaarl remount plus Chaaaaaaaarge!!'s shield outlasts your two-round reload, and his courage meter refills off minions — close the lane before he stacks two items.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin flip — Kled is a real level-1 bully and his mounted Bear Trap on a Rope grab plus aggression can win a blind trade, so don't shove face-first into the rope. The lane flips your way at 2-3: once you have Q, W and E you dash in with Quickdraw for the point-blank 4-shell spread, then dash back out before his Skaarl autos punish you. Dodge the telegraphed rope — if it whiffs he has no instant follow-up, and that's your free burst window. Last-hit safely with the tip of your Q powder trail when you can't commit.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin flip — Kled is a real level-1 bully and his mounted Bear Trap on a Rope grab plus aggression can win a blind trade, so don't shove face-first into the rope. The lane flips your way at 2-3: once you have Q, W and E you dash in with Quickdraw for the point-blank 4-shell spread, then dash back out before his Skaarl autos punish you. Dodge the telegraphed rope — it's 11 seconds at rank 1 and without it he has no instant follow-up, which is your free burst window. Last-hit from range with End of the Line when you can't commit.

edits.before: This is your takeover. Your Quickdraw armor from staying in combat and your second E charge compound through every extended trade, and Smoke Screen blinds his Skaarl autos so his trade-back whiffs. Bait the grab, eat the rope, then dash in, drop smoke, detonate Q and shred him before he can re-stack courage. At 6, Collateral Damage nukes him out of a fight he thought he won and, fired at a wall, escapes his R charge — this is where even trades become kills.
edits.after: This is your takeover. Quickdraw gives two True Grit stacks every time you dash AT him and your autos refresh the buff and cut its cooldown, so extended trades compound your way. Smoke Screen won't make his autos miss — it slows him on impact and cuts his sight, so use it to stop him repositioning. Bait the grab, then dash in, drop smoke, land End of the Line and shred him before he re-stacks courage. At 6, Collateral Damage nukes him out of a fight he thought he won.

edits.before: Drop Smoke Screen on him so his Skaarl autos miss and you win the extended trade blind
edits.after: Drop Smoke Screen on him for the impact slow and sight cut so he can't hold the extended trade

notes: The 'fire R at the wall behind you to escape Chaaaaaaaarge!!' line appeared in three places and is not a real mechanic — Collateral Damage does not displace Graves. I have removed it from whys[4], spikes[1] and dosFull[2].t; if the applier rejects any of those three the false escape survives in that spot and should be hand-checked. Also: the ownerKit derived flag on Graves' Q reads 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes', contradicting Riot's description — End of the Line detonates on terrain, it does not create any, and nothing I wrote relies on the flag.
